newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia seeks stake in Newmont's Batu Hijau mine.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia seeks stake in Newmont's Batu Hijau mine.

text.p: The Indonesian government has asked a subsidiary of U.S. Newmont Mining Corp for a stake in its copper and gold project in eastern Indonesia, Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Tuesday.
He said the government was seeking at least a 10-percent stake in PT Newmont Nusa Tenggara, which owns 80-percent of the Batu Hijau project in West Nusa Tenggara province.
"We feel that Newmont should give at least 10 percent of its share in Batu Hijau to the government," Sudjana told a news conference.
"It is a request. If they don't want to give, it's all right. We will still honour their contract," he said.
"Two national companies, Barito and Citra, have shown interest (in Batu Hijau)," he said. "But they have not made an official request to us."
Barito Pacific is controlled by timber baron Prajogo Pangestu while Citra Marga is headed by President Suharto's eldest daughter, Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana.
Sudjana said the government would not force Newmont to allocate the shares, adding that the request was made based on "nationalistic interests".

Government authorities are considering asking foreign mining companies to give the government a 10 percent stake in all future projects as part of a tightening in mining regulations following a scandal at the now worthless Busang gold project.

Busang, in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province, emerged as the biggest fraud in mining history following an independent consultants' report which concluded geological samples had been falsified and that Busang contained no economic gold deposit.

Sudjana, however, did not draw a direct link between the tightening in regulations and the government's request for 10 percent of Newmont's Batu Hijau project. Newmont Nusa president-director Eric Hamer said last Friday the company had not received any official request from the government to reduce its Batu Hijau stake.

He said, however, the work contract issued by the government in 1986 stated that Newmont Nusa had to offer for sale a fixed percentage of its shares to Indonesian companies between the sixth and 11th year of production at Batu Hijau.

Batu Hijau, which is expected to have a project life of 20 to 25 years, has yet to begin production, he said, adding that Newmont Nusa had invested $140 million in the project. The total cost of the project is expected to reach $2 billion.
He said Batu Hijau contains an estimated 5.3 million tonnes of copper and 13.4 million ounces of gold. Newmont's local partner, businessman Jusuf Merukh, has a 20-percent stake.

Merukh and Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd are locked in an ownership dispute over the Busang property. Bre-X had claimed in February to have found 71 million ounces of gold at Busang.
Hamer said Newmont Nusa had been waiting six months for government approval to begin constructing a mine at Batu Hijau despite having fulfilled the conditions.
Sudjana said the government was not delaying construction at Batu Hijau, adding that Newmont Nusa's application to begin developing the field was being processed.
"We are still processing their application," he said. Such things took time, he said.
He also said the government was considering requiring foreign companies to allocate at least a 10-percent stake in their projects to the government.
Sudjana said the condition might be set down in seventh-generation contracts of work being processed by his ministry.
